To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present an approximation method for computing thickness functions on binary shapes in any dimension that runs in O(n) time, where n is the number of points in the shape, and is guaranteed to be accurate up to a constant factor.

we provide a fast algorithm for computing the Euclidean thickness of a shape in arbitrary dimension, that our algorithm is based on the computation of the Euclidean distance function of a shape, and that the computation of the latter is done in a fast manner by means of the fast sweeping algorithm.
we provide a fast algorithm to compute an approximation of the Euclidian thickness distribution of a binary shape of any dimension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How can we approximate the local thickness distribution of a shape?
the following questions: How to compute a good approximation of the thickness distribution of a shape in arbitrary dimension?

- the definition of a fast approximation of the Euclidian thickness function of a binary shape; - the definition of an algorithm to compute such approximation; - the study of the accuracy of the approximation; - the definition and the implementation of an algorithm to estimate the Hausdorff distance between two shapes from their approximated thickness functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is fast and accurate for arbitrary dimensions.
our method can compute the thickness distribution of a shape with a time complexity of O(n log n) where n is the number of points of the shape.
the proposed algorithm is a fast, accurate and robust algorithm for the computation of the thickness distribution of binary shapes, in arbitrary dimension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a novel algorithm that computes a good approximation of the exact Euclidean thickness distribution in arbitrary dimensions, and that runs in time O(NlogN), where N is the number of points of the shape.
we present an efficient algorithm that approximates the exact Euclidean thickness distribution with any desired accuracy.
, we present an efficient and robust algorithm to approximate the Euclidean thickness of a binary shape by a piecewise linear function in arbitrary dimension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the computation can be reduced to the computation of the distance function to the boundary of the shape.
we provide a fast algorithm to compute an approximation of such thickness distribution.
, for a shape of size n and dimension d, the complexity is O(dn logn).
